pairs.subject: prompt-assembly
pairs.evidence: desk/src/lib/desk/hint.ts:166 The desk pipelines assemble prompts via ad-hoc string concatenation and late call-site string appending (`prompt + extra`) rather than through an owned, budgeted, and sealed layered prompt assembler.

techniques.evidence: desk/src/lib/desk/hint.ts:166 Prompts are constructed by string concatenation at individual call sites with post-construction appended strings (`prompt + extra`) rather than a dedicated assembler per prompt family.

desk/src/lib/desk/explain.ts:92 Prompt variables are interpolated via template strings with silent fallbacks to empty strings (`?? ""`) rather than declared typed contracts with loud failures on missing inputs.
desk/src/lib/desk/memory.ts:25 Learner memory notes are concatenated into prompts without a token budget, degradation ladder, or drop notices, bounded only by a raw array length cap in persistence.
desk/src/lib/desk/memory.ts:87 Model-written summary lines are saved to learner memory and injected into future prompts without source pointers or verification against session evidence.
desk/src/lib/rules/maths.ts:88 Maintains a single authored vocabulary mapping topic slip IDs to descriptions that is injected into prompts to constrain mistake naming to a closed vocabulary.
desk/src/lib/desk/hint.ts:147 Prompts open with persona and role priming ('You are...') instead of an actionable locate/done/check task envelope.
desk/src/lib/desk/items.ts:92 Requests are dispatched directly to the text engine without computing or recording a prompt fingerprint or cache key over the standing layers.
desk/src/lib/desk/items.ts:244 Dynamically documents only the active practice shapes for the given topic mapped from the topic path registry rather than listing all global shapes.

pairs.registryProposal: The standard should address educational tutoring systems where closed pedagogical error vocabularies (slips) act as a domain-specific house vocabulary layer to ground mistake diagnosis.

pairs.subject: prompt-assembly

techniques.evidence: desk/src/lib/english/conversation.ts:346 Composes prompts by string concatenations and dynamic JSON object spreading at the call site without an isolated, sealed assembler per prompt family.

desk/src/lib/english/conversation.ts:99 Applies hardcoded array slice limits without explicit token budget floors, degradation ladders, or notices naming omitted evidence.
desk/src/lib/english/conversation.ts:83 Opens the system prompt with persona and role priming ('You are Linga...') instead of an actionable locate/done/check envelope.

desk/src/lib/english/conversation.ts:84 Variables are embedded using inline ternary expressions and string interpolation rather than declared typed variable slots with explicit trust classifications.

pairs.registryProposal: The standard should distinguish conversational rehearsal contexts where domain safety policies (e.g. minor protection and age gating) trigger immediate conversation termination while pedagogical preference updates are deferred to subsequent scenes.
